blocks.text: A snapshot establishes ordered notification identities, the authoritative read marker, and a resume cursor. A stream adapter validates sequenced events, an idempotent reducer merges them in bounded transactions, and selectors derive the badge and virtualized rows without coupling correctness to paint timing.

Boundary checks:
- Clear separation of transport, reduction, and render.
- Event identity, monotonic sequence, and opaque resume cursor.
- One read-marker model shared by badge and panel.
- Gap recovery before cursor advancement.
- Batching that coalesces store commits without losing events.

blocks.title: Snapshot-to-projection path
blocks.text: Snapshot + resumable stream -> validator -> short ingest queue -> idempotent reducer -> normalized entities/read marker -> selectors -> virtualized list and badge. The scheduler controls commit frequency, not event retention.

blocks.title: Core building blocks
rows: Prefer WebSocket/SSE for push. Polling is fallback when sockets fail.
Buffer events to batch UI updates and handle bursts.
Drains the buffer on a cadence.
Drain a burst in one measured transaction while preserving every accepted event identity and sequence.
Owns the canonical list + unread state.
Owns normalized entities, ordered IDs, received event IDs, the contiguous cursor, and the versioned read marker.
Keeps DOM size small even if the feed contains hundreds/thousands.

steps.title: Panel open
steps.text: Render the virtualized list, batch accepted events, and project unread from entities plus the confirmed marker.

steps.title: Panel closed
steps.text: Stop rendering the list; keep reducing accepted events and derive the badge from entities plus the confirmed read marker.

blocks.text: Important: ingestion can be much faster than rendering. The scheduler is what keeps the UI stable.

blocks.title: Delivery, state, and projection boundaries
rows: Protocol frames become validated variants before normalized state changes
Unread derives from accepted sequence positions rather than render timing
Filters, panel visibility, and virtualization never mutate notification authority

blocks.title: Ordered notification projection
blocks.text: Make the notification path explicit: snapshot and resumable events enter one reducer, normalized entities and read markers produce a bounded visible feed, and components subscribe to stable selectors.
Worked example: reconnect across an unread boundary
The panel last reduced cursor c120 and the member read through notification n118. While offline, the server emits n121 through n124. Reconnect may replay n120 and deliver the new events in a burst.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Keep entities and read boundary; mark freshness stale.
Loss of transport does not erase evidence.
Open one stream with the last safely reduced cursor.
Show reconnecting without a blocking spinner.
Counts and rows do not change.
Batch normalize, order by server sequence, then compute unread from the stable boundary.
One update and a concise new-items affordance appear.
Unread does not depend on render timing.
